quiz.question: What do electrons do when there is no external push applied to them?

answers.answer: They flow steadily in one direction
They vibrate randomly in place without useful movement
They stop moving entirely and become still
They escape from the atom and float freely

quiz.explanation: Without a push, electrons just vibrate randomly in place. They don't produce any useful flow. A push is needed to get them moving in a consistent direction.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a source that can push electrons to flow?

answers.answer: Friction from rubbing a balloon on hair

quiz.explanation: The lesson mentions three sources that push electrons: batteries (chemical energy), generators (spinning magnets), and friction (like rubbing a balloon on hair). Solar panels were not discussed in this lesson.
